blocks.text: As pressure mounts, fear begins to work inside Sikh society as well as outside it. Mothers asked them to have their hair shorn and disappear among the Jats, urging the young to save themselves by blending back into village life before the dragnet tightened further.
Not everyone accepts that counsel. The true Khalsa remained, even as wavering men fell away and families tried to pull sons and brothers back from what looked like certain destruction.

Among those who stayed, the debate turned to strategy rather than surrender. The elders' advice favored mobility over grand display, urging the Singhs to survive by sudden strikes, dispersal, and return instead of offering themselves up in one doomed stand.
